full_judgment:
4. The opposite party No. 1 entered appearance in the said Execution Case and on 28-11-2004 filed an application under Order XXI rule 29 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the Court of District Judge, Dhaka for stay of the execution proceedings stating that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff earlier instituted Title Suit No. 367 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 40 before the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka challenging the legality of the Arbitral Awards passed by the International Court of Arbitration and, as such, it is required to stay all further proceeding of the Execution Case till disposal of the aforesaid two Title Suits. 

 5. The Court of District Judge, Dhaka upon hearing the said application was pleased to stay all further proceedings of the said Execution Case pending disposal of Title Suit No. 367 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 40 of 2004 by his order dated 27-9-20-05 stating as follows: 

 6. The petitioner-company after being unsuccessful in taking all possible efforts to get the aforesaid title suits heard, on 19-6-2008 filed an application for vacating the order of stay dated 27-9-2005 before the Court of learned District Judge, Dhaka stating, inter-alia, that the learned District Judge, Dhaka had acted without jurisdiction in allowing the application for stay of the execution proceeding till disposal of Title Suit No. 367 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 40 of 2004 pending before the leaned Joint District Judge, Dhaka. It has been also stated in the application that the consent of the lawyers cannot grant jurisdiction inasmuch as jurisdiction of a Court is created by statute, it can neither be conferred nor taken away by consent of the parties or their lawyers. 

 7. The opposite party No. 1 resisted the said application for vacating the order of stay by filing a written objection contending that the learned District Judge, Dhaka in the facts and circumstance of the case committed no illegality in allowing the application for stay all further proceedings of the Execution Case No. 4 of 2004 till disposal of Title Suit No. 367 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 40 of 2004 by order dated 27-9-2005. 

 8. The learned District Judge, Dhaka after hearing both the parties rejected the application of the petitioner for vacating the order of stay by the impugned order No. 17 dated 27-8-2008 mainly on, two grounds that the petitioner had not objected at the time of hearing the application for staying proceeding of the Execution Case No. 4 of 2004 pending disposal of Title Suit No. 367 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 40 of 2004 and in the attending facts and circumstances of the case the complications may arise if the order of stay dated 27-9-2005 is vacated. 

 10. Mr Abdur Razzaque, the learned Advocate appearing for the award-holder-petitioner submits that order XXI rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure clearly provides for staying the execution of a decree till the disposal of the pending suit is only attracted when the subsequent suit is pending before the same Court who passed the decree in the previous suit and it must be filed by the judgment debtor which is lacking in the present case but the Court of District Judge, Dhaka having failed to appreciate this simple legal aspect of the case and thereby seriously erred in law in passing the impugned order without properly applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr Razzaque to fortify his submission has relied on the decisions reported in 4 BLC 615 and 53 DLR 610. 

 11. Mr Tufailur Rahman, the learned Advocate on the other hand appearing for the opposite party NO. 2 by filing counter affidavit support the impugned order which was, according to him just, correct and proper. He is the course of argument after placing the impugned order and other materials on record submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case the learned District Judge committed no illegality in allowing the application for staying all further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of the pending suits. 

 12. Now, let us examine first how far the learned District Judge, Dhaka was justified in allowing the application for staying all further proceedings of the execution case No. 4 of 2004 till disposal of the Title Suit No. 367 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 40 of 2004 pending before the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka. 

 13. It is found that the petitioner in order to enforce the Awards of the International Court of Arbitration in Bangladesh on 10-8-2004 filed Money Execution Case No. 4 of 2004 before the Court of District Judge, Dhaka for recovery of Taka 84,75,44,524.80 along with interest in accordance with section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and prior to the said Execution Case the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff had filed two separate suits being Title Suit No. 367 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 40 of 2004 before the Joint District Judge, Dhaka Challenging the legality of the Arbitral Awards passed by the International Court of Arbitration. In this connection the relevant provisions of law are required to be referred to for having a better view of the dispute in question. 

 "Where a suit is pending in any Court against the holder of a decree of such Court, on the part of the person against whom the decree was passed, the Court may, on such terms as to security or otherwise, as it things fit, stay execution of the decree until the pending suit has been decided." 

 15. From a reading of the above quoted provisions, it transpires that an application for staying the execution of a decree till disposal of the pending suit is only attracted when the subsequent suit is pending before the same Court who passed the decree in the previous suit and it must be filed by the judgment-debtor. 

 "I read again the provision of rule 29 of Order XXI of the Code. It says "where a suit is pending in any Court against the holder of a decree of such Court, on the part of the person against whom the decree was passed, the Court may, on such terms as to security or otherwise as it thinks it, stay execution of the decree until the pending suit has been decided. "This power has been clearly given to an Executing Court as well as to the Court in which suit impeaching the decree is pending if the decree is a decree of this Court." 

 18. In this case we have already noticed that the Title Suit No. 367 of 2002 and title Suit No. 40 of 2004 are pending before the joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka and the Arbitral Awards sought to be enforced by the District Judge has been passed by the International Court of Arbitration which is different from the Court before whom the aforesaid suits are pending Moreover, in order to invoke Order XXI rule 29 Of the Code of Civil Procedure, the existence of a decree is required and admittedly, the Arbitral Award sought to be enforced is neither a decree nor the same has been deemed to be a decree by any law. Therefore, in the facts of the case and the principles enunciated in the cited decisions vis-à-vis the provision of Order XXI rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure we have no hesitation to hold that the learned District Judge, Dhaka committed serious error of law in passing, the impugned order without property applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the Subject and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 20. Mr Tufailur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 2, Upon referring to the order sheets of the learned District Judge, Dhaka submits that the learned District Judge was pleased to allow the application for staying all further proceedings of the Money Execution Case No. 4 of 2004 till disposal of the Title Suit No. 367 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 40 of 2004 by his order dated 27-9-2005 mainly on the basis of the consent of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and thereafter, keeping silent over a period of two years and nine months it does not lie in the mouth of the petitioner that the Court of learned District Judge having failed to consider whether it has jurisdiction to pass the Order of Stay under Order XXI rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 22. To resolve this dispute we have studied the cited decision to the best of our ability and find in those decision our Appellate Division consistently held that the jurisdiction of Courts is created by statutes and that it can neither be conferred nor taken away by agreement or concession of parties to the litigation or of their lawyers. So, we are unable to see eye to eye to such submission made by Mr Tufailur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 2.
